recipes.name: Ox bone soup (Seolleongtang)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef flank (or brisket or round)
1½ pounds Korean radish (or daikon radish), peeled
Water (14 cups for the initial boil, then about 12 cups for each batch of broth)
1 cup shredded cooked beef (from the soup)
A pinch of ground black pepper
instructions: Soak the ox bones and the beef in cold water for 20 minutes to remove any blood.
Rinse the bones a couple of times in cold water to remove any bone chips. Drain the water.
Bring 14 cups of water (3½ quarts) to a boil in a large pot.
Carefully add the bones and beef to the boiling water. Boil for about 10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and take out the bones and beef. Get rid of the water.
Rinse and drain the meat in cold water to remove the excess fat.
If you only have one pot to use, clean it thoroughly with kitchen soap.
Return the bones and the beef to the pot.
Add about 12 cups of water (3 quarts), 1 medium onion, and 1½ pounds of peeled radish to the pot. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
After about 20 to 30 minutes, when the water starts boiling, lower the heat to simmer for 3 hours.
Turn off the heat and take the beef and radish out of the pot. Leave the bones behind.
Put the beef and radish into a bowl.

Pour the brownish broth into a large heatproof bowl. Cool it quickly in an ice-water bath and refrigerate. Continue cooking the bones in fresh water, cooling each new batch of broth before combining it with the chilled broth. If you have a larger pot, you could keep boiling the bones and adding water over hours and hours, but with a small pot we need to do it in stages and collect in this collecting bowl.
Fill the pot with water again (about 3 quarts) and boil over medium-high for about 20 minutes. When it starts boiling, lower the heat and simmer for 2½ to 3 hours.
Turn off the heat, open the lid, and pour the broth into the collecting bowl. It will be a lot whiter than the first time we poured it out.
Fill your pot with water again and boil over medium-high heat for about 20 minutes. When it starts boiling, lower the heat and simmer for 2½ to 3 hours.
Turn off the heat, open the lid, and pour the broth into the collecting bowl. This time it will be really white, but thin.
Once all the broth has been collected and cooled, cover and refrigerate for several hours or overnight until the fat on top solidifies. Skim off the fat before reheating and serving.
Take the bone soup out of the fridge. Remove the solid fat from the top with a spoon or strainer.
Thinly slice the cooked beef about ⅛ inch thick and the radish about ¼ inch thick.
Reheat the bone soup and ladle the soup into a serving bowl.
Add a few slices of the beef and radish to the soup. Serve with warm rice and kimchi, along with chopped green onions, minced garlic, kosher salt, and ground black pepper.

Add some salt, chopped green onion, and ground black pepper to the soup. Mix it well with your spoon. You can add warm rice to the soup and enjoy!Tip: Season the soup with a little salt at first, then add more to taste. Everyone can season their own bowl just the way they like it!
For one serving, shred 1 cup of the cooked beef into thin strips and place it in a mixing bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons chopped green onion, 2 teaspoons soy sauce, 2 teaspoons hot pepper flakes, a pinch of ground black pepper, and 2 teaspoons toasted sesame oil. Mix well with a spoon.
Ladle the boiling soup into a serving bowl and add a few slices of radish and the mixture of seasoned beef.
Serve with warm rice, kosher salt, and kimchi.
